findings.highlight: the bicycle passing by me stopped to make way for me
findings.evidenceJa: 道を譲ろうとした自転車が急に止まったかと思うと
findings.explanation: Haruki tries to yield to the bicycle, which then stops suddenly. The English reverses the direction of courtesy and says the bicycle stops to make way for Haruki.
findings.japanese:
道を譲ろうとした自転車が急に止まったかと思うと、
聞き覚えのある声が俺を呼んだ。
findings.todokanai: I thought the bicycle passing by me stopped to make way for me, yet its rider spoke with a voice I recognized.

findings.highlight: this is something they don't want their children to see
findings.evidenceJa: 聞かせたくない話も辞さないという意志
findings.explanation: Haruki infers that the parents are resolved not to shrink from scenes or conversation they would never want their children to witness. The English merely says the matter is something they do not want the children to see or hear, omitting the parents' deliberate readiness to proceed.
findings.japanese:
つまりそれは、自分たちの子供には見せたくない場面も…
聞かせたくない話も辞さないという意志なのかもしれない。
findings.todokanai: In other words, this is something they don't want their children to see… and a conversation they don't want them to hear.

findings.highlight: we ran into some obstacles
findings.evidenceJa: 少しヘコむことがあったのは本当だけど、でも今までだって、何度もこういうことあった
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she personally suffered a discouraging blow, but has faced this kind of thing many times before and survived it. The English turns her recurring emotional collapses into obstacles jointly encountered by the relationship.
findings.japanese:
「確かに、少しヘコむことがあったのは本当だけど、
でも今までだって、何度もこういうことあった。
…何度も切り抜けてきたんだよ」
findings.todokanai: "True, we ran into some obstacles, but we've had plenty of those before… and we've always overcome them."

findings.highlight: unwarranted trust
findings.evidenceJa: その、無償の信頼が
findings.explanation: 無償の信頼 is the mother's unconditional, freely given trust in Haruki. 'Unwarranted trust' calls it unjustified or foolish, replacing the source's emphasis on generosity with retrospective judgment.
findings.japanese: その、無償の信頼が…
findings.todokanai: That unwarranted trust…

findings.highlight: you loved Setsuna from the bottom of your heart
findings.evidenceJa: 心の底から雪菜を一番に考えてくれている、嫌になるくらい信頼できる男
findings.explanation: Setsuna's father trusted Haruki as a man who, from the bottom of his heart, always put Setsuna first. The English reduces this to loving her, omitting the precise priority Haruki has now betrayed.
findings.japanese:
「そういう言葉では、絶対に娘を諭せない…
心の底から雪菜を一番に考えてくれている、
嫌になるくらい信頼できる男だと思っていたから…っ」
findings.todokanai: "But those weren't words I could tell my daughter… because I thought that you loved Setsuna from the bottom of your heart. I thought you were a man I could trust…!"

findings.highlight: "I'm going to… Vienna. I'm sorry for all the trouble I've caused you."
findings.evidenceJa:
「ウィーンに…行きます。
今まで色々と、お世話になりました」
findings.explanation: 今まで色々と、お世話になりました is a formal expression of gratitude for all the family's past care, not an apology for trouble caused — The line still functions as Haruki's final farewell.
findings.japanese:
「ウィーンに…行きます。
今まで色々と、お世話になりました」
findings.todokanai: "I'm going to… Vienna. I'm sorry for all the trouble I've caused you."

findings.highlight: didn't allow me to speak about what happened
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜は、有無を言わせてくれなかった
findings.explanation: Setsuna brooks no objection while treating Haruki's injury. The English invents a refusal to let him discuss what happened, changing determined first aid into active suppression of the confrontation.
findings.japanese: 雪菜は、有無を言わせてくれなかった。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna didn't allow me to speak about what happened.

findings.highlight: replace it with a different kind of happiness
findings.evidenceJa: 同じ大きさの、違う幸せを積み上げていくことになる
findings.explanation: Setsuna believed she and Haruki would accumulate a different happiness of the same magnitude as the lost happiness of the trio. 'Replace it' omits both gradual accumulation and the crucial claim of equal scale.
findings.japanese:
「だから春希くんと二人で、同じ大きさの、
違う幸せを積み上げていくことになるんだって。
一緒に、生きていくんだって、そう信じてた…」
findings.todokanai: "That's why I thought I could replace it with a different kind of happiness with just the two of us. I believed we could live together…"

findings.highlight: even greater than what we had five years ago
findings.evidenceJa: 今と同じくらい、ううん、それ以上の大きな幸せに包まれるだけだよ
findings.explanation: Setsuna says the happiness of the trio five years ago was as great as her present happiness with Haruki—no, even greater. The English instead makes the proposed happiness greater than what they had five years ago, reversing which state is the benchmark.
findings.japanese:
「ただ、５年前の…
今と同じくらい、ううん、
それ以上の大きな幸せに包まれるだけだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Because all we have to do is… wrap ourselves in a happiness that's even greater than what we had five years ago."

findings.highlight: yet also indecisive at the same time
findings.evidenceJa: どっちつかずでもない、どっちとも深く繋がってしまう人生
findings.explanation: Haruki says this would not be a life of mere indecision; it would be a life deeply bound to both women. The English calls him indecisive, erasing the distinction that explains why the arrangement would injure both.
findings.japanese:
そんな、どっちつかずでもない、
どっちとも深く繋がってしまう人生は、
俺の世界で一番大切な二人を不幸にしてしまう。
findings.todokanai: I'd only end up making the two people I care about more than anyone else in the world completely miserable, chaining them to myself in a limbo where I'm closely tied to the both of them, yet also indecisive at the same time.

findings.highlight: use different means
findings.evidenceJa: たとえ目的と手段を入れ替えてでも
findings.explanation: Haruki is prepared to invert purpose and means—to make his exclusion of Setsuna serve the choice of a future with Kazusa. The English reduces this morally perverse inversion to using different means.
findings.japanese:
…たとえ目的と手段を入れ替えてでも、
雪菜まで、先の見えない未来に巻き込むわけにはいかない。
findings.todokanai: …Even if it means I have to use different means… I cannot involve Setsuna in a future without light at the end of the tunnel.

findings.highlight: She's giving me up to Kazusa.
findings.evidenceJa: どこまでも、俺に、かずさに譲歩する
findings.explanation: Setsuna keeps conceding to both Haruki and Kazusa by offering to join them on their terms. She is not simply surrendering Haruki to Kazusa; her proposed three-person life still includes herself.
findings.japanese: どこまでも、俺に、かずさに譲歩する。
findings.todokanai: She's giving me up to Kazusa.

findings.highlight: "I don't need any of them!"
findings.evidenceJa: 「そんなのなくしたっていい！」
findings.explanation: Setsuna says she would be willing to lose family and friends, rather than that she presently needs none of them — Her readiness to sacrifice every external bond for the trio remains.
findings.japanese: 「そんなのなくしたっていい！」
findings.todokanai: "I don't need any of them!"

findings.highlight: Kazusa is a tumbleweed
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜が樹木なら、かずさは浮き草だ
findings.explanation: Kazusa is 浮き草, a floating aquatic plant or duckweed, contrasted with Setsuna as a rooted tree. 'Tumbleweed' breaks the next lines' water-and-nutrient logic and substitutes an arid image for the source's aquatic dependence.
findings.japanese:
雪菜が樹木なら、かずさは浮き草だ。
地面に根を張って強く生きていくことはできないんだ。
findings.todokanai: If Setsuna is a tree that plants roots, then Kazusa is a tumbleweed. It's just not possible for her to extend her roots and live firmly.

findings.highlight: find water to sustain herself little by little as she goes
findings.evidenceJa: 水から少しずつ栄養をもらって生きていくしかない
findings.explanation: As floating weed, Kazusa can only live by taking nourishment little by little from the water itself while cut off from earth and world. The English makes her travel in search of water, continuing the erroneous tumbleweed metaphor.
findings.japanese:
地面と、世界と隔絶したところで、
水から少しずつ栄養をもらって生きていくしかないんだ。
findings.todokanai: She must find water to sustain herself little by little as she goes, separated both from the ground and the world.

findings.highlight: 'my body' doesn't belong to 'only' myself anymore
findings.evidenceJa: お前『の体』はもう、お前『だけ』のものじゃない
findings.explanation: Haruki corrects Kazusa by saying, 'Your body isn't yours alone anymore.' The English changes both possessors to Haruki and has him talk about his own body.
findings.japanese:
「お前『の体』はもう、
お前『だけ』のものじゃない、だろ。
必要な部分まで省略するな」
findings.todokanai: "You mean to say that 'my body' doesn't belong to 'only' myself anymore. Don't neglect the important parts."

findings.highlight: I could push her down
findings.evidenceJa: 強く押し倒し、全身でのしかかって拘束し、激しくその身体をまさぐっても
findings.explanation: The ても sequence describes concrete acts Haruki performs—forcing Kazusa down, pinning her with his body, and groping her—before the apodosis at line 567 says she still relaxes and accepts him. Repeated 'I could' wording turns the enacted assaultive contact into a hypothetical possibility.
findings.japanese:
強く押し倒し、全身でのしかかって拘束し、
激しくその身体をまさぐっても。
findings.todokanai: I could push her down with all my force and lean my body over her. I could experience the sensation of her body.

findings.highlight: call me out on it
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が迷うたびに、何度も振り回して
findings.explanation: Haruki apologizes for jerking Kazusa around over and over whenever he wavers. The English instead asks Kazusa to call him out, turning his admission of harm into an instruction for her future behavior.
findings.japanese:
「ごめんな、かずさ。
俺が迷うたびに、何度も振り回して」
findings.todokanai: "I'm sorry, Kazusa… Every time I lose my way, call me out on it."

findings.highlight: Let me be of some use.
findings.evidenceJa: 少しでも、あたしを必要としてくれよ
findings.explanation: Kazusa asks Haruki to need her, even a little. 'Let me be of some use' changes her plea for emotional necessity into utility, precisely the reduction her painkiller metaphor has made painful.
findings.japanese:
「だから、せめてあたしの胸で泣いてくれ。
少しでも、あたしを必要としてくれよ」
findings.todokanai: "Then at least cry in my arms. Let me be of some use."

findings.highlight: The amount of suffering we've caused to so many people
findings.evidenceJa: あれだけ多くの人を踏み台にした意味がない
findings.explanation: Haruki says that otherwise there would have been no point in using so many people as stepping stones. The English replaces his ruthless, self-aware instrumentalization of others with the more passive suffering they caused.
findings.japanese: でないと、あれだけ多くの人を踏み台にした意味がない。
findings.todokanai: The amount of suffering we've caused to so many people would have been for nothing otherwise.

findings.highlight: For a while, I listened in drowsiness
findings.evidenceJa: しばらく後、かずさが呟いたその言葉を、俺は夢うつつで聞いていた
findings.explanation: Kazusa murmurs the words some time later, and Haruki hears them half-asleep. The English attaches しばらく to how long he listened rather than when she spoke.
findings.japanese:
しばらく後、かずさが呟いたその言葉を、
俺は夢うつつで聞いていた。
findings.todokanai: For a while, I listened in drowsiness to Kazusa's whispers.
